title: Lord, We Come Before Thee Now
description: Lord, We Come Before Thee Now in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Hammond wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 22 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Blessing humbly requested”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, we come be-fore thee now; At thy feet we hum-bly bow; O, do not our suit dis-dain; Shall we seek thee, Lord, in vain?

lines: Lord, we come before thee now;
At thy feet we humbly bow;
O, do not our suit disdain;
Shall we seek thee, Lord, in vain?
Now we seek thee; here we stay;
Lord, from hence we would not go,
Comfort those who weep and mourn;
Let the time of joy return;
Those that are cast down, lift up;
Make them strong in faith and hope.
Grant that all may seek and find
Heal the sick; the captive free;
Let us all rejoice in thee.

licence: Public domain: William Hammond died in 1783.
credits: Words by William Hammond (1719–1783), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
